- Astronomers report the first observationally confirmed atmosphere around a rocky exoplanet within its star's habitable zone, after detecting helium escaping from the upper atmosphere of LHS 1140 b, a super-Earth approximately 49 light-years from Earth. [src: (Space.com)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 22
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The Jordanian military reports that air defenses have intercepted 8 out of 10 projectiles fired by Iran against the country in Aqaba near the Israeli border, with two missiles landing in remote areas. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (CBC)] [src: (Ynetnews)]
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
- The General Staff of the Kuwait Army reports that Kuwait's military and air defenses have been actively intercepting "hostile drones" from Iran. [src: (Arab Times Kuwait)] [src: (The Times Kuwait)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The United States military launches Tomahawk missile strikes on Iran's Larak Island. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
- The U.S. Central Command launches a new round of strikes against Iran, marking the 12th consecutive day of attacks. [src: (AP)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Financial Times reports that the tanker Kavomalaes, belonging to Greek shipowner George Prokopiou, was "highly likely" to have been captured in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran two days earlier. [src: (Forbes)]
- Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet announces that they have killed three Hamas militants in the northern Gaza Strip, including one in the Hamas military wing that took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Cleveland Jewish News)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Seven oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia's port of Yanbu change course away from the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb after the Houthis announced a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports. [src: (The Washington Post)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- 2026 Kabul hospital airstrike
- Amnesty International calls for an investigation into a Pakistani airstrike against a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul, Afghanistan, as a possible war crime. [src: (The Washington Post)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- UNICEF reports that six people, including two children, have been killed and 30 people including children have been injured in a drone strike on a market in Al-Rahad, North Kordofan, Sudan. [src: (AA)]
- A Chadian official reports that a drone attack from Sudanese territory has attacked positions in Chad, injuring civilians and destroying vehicles and several shops. The attack is the fifth in recent months, following an incursion by Rapid Support Forces last January. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
- Sixteen civilians, most of whom gold miners, are killed during a village attack suspected to have been perpetrated by ADF forces in Mandeite locality, Mambasa, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AA)]
- Southern Thailand insurgency
- Five soldiers are killed and six civilians are injured in a mass shooting by ten unknown gunmen at a security checkpoint in Narathiwat province, Thailand. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
- A 35-year-old head constable is shot and killed in a militant attack in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India. The Resistance Front claims responsibility. [src: (NDTV)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, rise to over US$95 and $86 per barrel, respectively, and the United States average gasoline price rises to $4.06 per gallon, amidst the ongoing conflict. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (NBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Seven people are killed after a truck collides with a medical transport van in Pernambuco, Brazil. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A Robinson R44 helicopter crashes in Sincan, Ankara, Turkey, killing the pilot and injuring the co-pilot. [src: (Turkiye Today)]
- In the United States, West Virginia governor Patrick Morrisey declares a state of emergency and announces that 100 National Guard troops have been deployed after flash floods caused by torrential rains were reported across the state, including the northern part. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Independent)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- The death toll from the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh exceeds 800. [src: (The Business Standard)] [src: (Dhaka Tribune)]
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- African CDC director Jean Kaseya reports that the death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached past 1,000. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The number of reported cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. state of Michigan exceeds 7,000. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (WDIV)]
- The fire department of Tokyo, Japan, reports 453 heat-related hospitalizations, its highest daily total since records began in 2010, as a severe heat wave kills one person and leaves four critically ill. The country's Fire and Disaster Management Agency reports at least 14 heat-related deaths nationwide over the previous week. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
International relations
- Saudi Arabia–United States relations, Nuclear program of Saudi Arabia
- Saudi Arabia and the United States sign a civil nuclear cooperation agreement allowing Saudi Arabia to use U.S. reactor technology, enrich uranium, and reprocess nuclear waste. The pact excludes the IAEA Additional Protocol and proceeds to U.S. congressional review. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Stabbing of Salman Rushdie
- The federal trial against Hadi Matar, the man who attempted to kill author Salman Rushdie in August 2022 in New York, United States, opens. If he is convicted, Matar faces a sentence of life in prison. He is already serving a 25-year state prison sentence in New York. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Unknown gunmen open fire at a police station in Canindeyú Department, Paraguay, killing three officers and wounding another. [src: (Abc.com)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi is released after police detained him outside prime minister Narendra Modi's residence yesterday during protests demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and changes to the examination system. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Catholic Church in China
- Pope Leo XIV consecrates Fr. Joseph Chang Yanfeng as the bishop of Chifeng in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China under the 2018 provisional framework, which cedes authority over its bishops to the Chinese government. [src: (Holy See)] [src: (Vatican News)]
Science and technology
- Exomoon candidates
- The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope reports evidence of a possible exomoon-like object orbiting the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 B in the CD-35 2722 system, in a study published in the Nature journal. [src: (Space.com)] [src: (Phys.org)] [src: (Nature)]
|

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 24
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- Bahrain's military says that they have intercepted a number of missiles and drones from Iran. [src: (Arab News)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- Jordan's military says that they have intercepted seven missiles and six drones launched from Iran. No casualties or damage were reported. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- Kuwait's army says that its air defenses confronted several attacks from Iran. [src: (Arab News)]
- Iran says it has attacked U.S. military bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait, including the Isa Air Base, using Arash drones. [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The U.S. military says its forces fired into a tanker's engine room and disabled the vessel after its crew repeatedly attempted to breach the American blockade of Iranian ports and ignored warnings. [src: (AFP via BSS)]
- The Indian embassy in Tehran reports that the Mozambique-flagged LPG tanker Disha with 28 Indian nationals on the vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. All 28 crew members were reported safe. [src: (The Hindustan Times)] [src: (India Today)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The United States strikes an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy naval academy in Ziba Kenar, Gilan province, Iran. [src: (Arab News)] [src: (Iran International)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
- Drones target Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan Region, with six drones reported to be intercepted. [src: (AP)] [src: (Kurdistan24)]
- The Wall Street Journal reports that Bahraini and Kuwaiti fighter jets attacked military targets inside Iran earlier in July, with air and intelligence support from the United Arab Emirates. [src: (The Wall Street Journal)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military reports that the air force has struck Hamas weapon depots, weapon manufacturing sites and tunnels in the Gaza Strip, and accuses the militant group of violating the ceasefire signed in October 2025. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- July 2026 West Bank unrest
- Clashes in Tell, Nablus, kill four Palestinians and two Israelis after a confrontation between settlers and locals in the town. Subsequent settler attacks in the West Bank injure at least 10 Palestinians. [src: (Haaretz)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- The Houthis deny reports that they have closed the Bab-el-Mandeb and state that they are not seeking to close it, reaffirming that they have only established a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. [src: (DW)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi military sites in Hodeidah, Yemen, after a long hiatus in response to the movement's attacks on maritime shipping, while the militant group vows to retaliate. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries warehouses
- A Wildberries logistic hub in Russia-occupied Crimea is hit by Ukrainian drones and catches fire. [src: (RBC-Ukraine)]
- Ukrainian drones also hit Wildberries logistics hubs in Saint Petersburg and Tver, Russia. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Kyiv strikes
- Ukrainian officials say a Russian ballistic missile strike on a private training ground hosting a defence-industry event in the Kyiv Oblast killed 10 people and injured nearly 100. Prosecutors investigate possible negligence in organizing the event. [src: (Reuters)]
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Romanian F-16 ​fighter jet shot down a Russian Geran-2 drone near Padina, Buzău County, that had entered its airspace for the first ‌time. [src: (Euronews)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The North Kordofan government reports that 15 civilians in the Burbur area south of El-Obeid, Sudan have been killed by a Rapid Support Forces drone strike. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- At least 27 people are killed, including 12 militants, in an attack on a security check post in Tank District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. [src: (Hindustan Times)]
Business and economy
- Tariffs in the second Trump administration
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, ceremonially opens, with Canadian officials marking the opening ceremony of the bridge with the absence of American officials amidst ongoing trade tensions. [src: (Detroit Free Press)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
- Paramount announces that they have agreed to delay its US$111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery amidst lawsuits from twelve U.S. state attorneys general. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (The Hill)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- 2026 France wildfires
- French authorities evacuate more than 110,000 people from Cap Ferret, Gironde, by land and sea as an uncontrolled wildfire burns over 19,000 hectares, destroys 80 homes, and threatens the peninsula’s only access road. [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Spain wildfires
- Spanish interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska declares a national emergency over wildfires in the Community of Madrid and the Province of Ávila, placing the Military Emergencies Unit in command. Authorities evacuate more than 10,000 people as three major fires remain uncontrolled. [src: (AA)]
- The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 72. [src: (The Guardian)] 
- Thirteen people are killed and two others are injured after a heavy boulder rolled down a hill and hit moving vehicles in Chamba District, India. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five people are killed and three others are injured when a soil collapse buries a house in Hongtong County, Shanxi, China. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Oxford University reports the first volunteer that has been injected with the Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain of Ebola that is causing a outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AFP via GMA News Online)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, has spread to an additional four states: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Pennsylvania. [src: (CNBC)]
- The U.S. state of Michigan surpasses 8,100 cases of cyclosporiasis. [src: (CBS News)]
- Dengue fever outbreaks
- The Sudan Doctors Union reports a dengue fever outbreak in Sudan's Blue Nile state, killing 39 people and leaving 300 infected. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Measles resurgence in the United States
- The U.S. CDC reports 2,318 confirmed measles cases in the country during the first seven months of 2026, marking the highest annual total since 1991. [src: (AFP via Euractiv)]
International relations
- International sanctions against Iran
- Iran–European Union relations
- The European Union sanctions five Iranian judges over alleged human rights violations and Ashiyane cyber group founder Nima Salehi, whom it accuses of cooperating with Iranian authorities to suppress information. [src: (Reuters)]
- United States sanctions against Iran
- The U.S. treasury department announces sanctions against nine firms and four people associated with sanctioned Iranian financer Babak Zanjani after attempting to evade previous sanctions. [src: (Reuters)]
- International Criminal Court investigation in Venezuela
- Venezuelan foreign minister Félix Plasencia says the country will withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged geographic bias. The ICC says it has not received formal notice and that existing investigations and cooperation obligations remain unaffected. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Mexico–United States relations, Mexican war on drugs
- The U.S. state department, in coordination with the Mexican finance ministry, sanctions over 50 Mexican individuals and companies allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. [src: (Bloomberg)] [src: (El País)]
Law and crime
- 2020 Phala Phala robbery
- A South African court temporarily halts the parliament's impeachment inquiry into president Cyril Ramaphosa over the theft of US$580,000 from his farm, pending his challenge to a report finding possible constitutional violations. [src: (Reuters)]
- Karolkiewicz family murders
- Eight people are killed, including six children, in an arson and shooting attack at a house in Grand Haven Charter Township, Michigan, United States. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (The Indian Express)]
- Diplomatic sources say International Criminal Court member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Ahmad Khan following sexual misconduct allegations. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (CNN)]
- Prosecutors say thieves stole a 2,500-year-old gold Celtic necklace from the Musée du Pays Châtillonnais in Châtillon-sur-Seine, Côte-d'Or, France, after breaking its display case during opening hours. The artifact belongs to the Vix treasure. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Politics and elections
- Protests against the dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
- For the ninth consecutive day, thousands continue to protest in Kyiv, Ukraine, demanding Mykhailo Fedorov's reinstatement as Minister of Defence. [src: (The Kyiv Independent)]
- Bangladeshi president Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns from office, citing health reasons. [src: (Reuters)]
- Forty deputies of the Polish Sejm leave the Law and Justice party as part of a dispute between party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and member Mateusz Morawiecki. [src: (AP)] [src: (Polsat )]
Science and technology
- The SpaceX Starship test flight 13, the first to successfully deploy operational Starlink satellites, successfully lands in the Indian Ocean intact. [src: (CNN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 26
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
- Iran and the United States submit their responses to a proposal by Pakistan and Qatar to resume talks between the two countries. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has prevented six ships from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (CNBC)]
- Iranian media reports that an oil tanker exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after it has hit a naval mine. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Gaza war
- Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war
- Five aid convoys from the United Arab Emirates carrying 938 tonnes of humanitarian aid arrive in Gaza as part of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3. [src: (Gulf Today)] [src: (Sharjah24)]
- The Israeli military states that an Hamas unmanned aerial vehicle unit commander was killed in an airstrike yesterday in central Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Red Sea crisis
- Eleven vessels cross the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, according to shipping data from Kpler. [src: (Reuters)]
- Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- The Houthis shoot down a Saudi Arabian reconnaissance drone in northwest Yemen. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announces that they have recaptured the North Kordofan areas of Umm Qarfa and Juraikh. The SAF also seize control of the National Export Highway which connects Sudan's capital Khartoum and North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Horizon)] [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- At least 30 people are killed and others are injured in an attack on a community by unknown gunmen in Kaura, Kaduna State, Nigeria. [src: (CTV News)]
Arts and culture
- UNESCO designates the Alamut Castle in Qazvin province, Iran, a World Heritage Site. [src: (Tehran Times)]
Disasters and accidents
- Vietnamese cargo ship sinks in the South China Sea along the Vietnamese coast. Forty-five people are rescued while 17 more are still missing. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- Argentina–Brazil relations
- Brazil recalls its ambassador to Argentina and summons Argentina's ambassador after Argentine president Javier Milei made remarks deemed derogatory about Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Supreme Court justice Alexandre de Moraes at a political event in São Paulo. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Iran–Ukraine relations, Ukraine in the 2026 Iran war
- The Iranian foreign ministry summons the Ukrainian chargé d'affaires in Tehran over an attack by Ukraine on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea that killed an Iranian sailor, calling it a "hostile and criminal act". [src: (CNBC)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Berlin Pride attack
- A suspect in a recent vehicle-ramming and mass stabbing attack in Berlin, identified as a 21-year-old German citizen of Lebanese descent, is shot and killed by police after allegedly rushing toward officers with a weapon. [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 Seattle Center shooting
- Three people are killed and four others are injured in a shooting during the annual Bite of Seattle festival in Seattle, Washington, United States. [src: (CNN)]
Politics and elections
- 2027 Salvadoran presidential election
- El Salvador's Nationalist Republican Alliance nominates former legislator Mayteé Iraheta for president, while the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front nominates physician Rafael Aguirre. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- International Space Station expeditions
- Expedition 74, the joint NASA–Roscosmos–ESA expedition aboard the International Space Station, ends after the Soyuz MS-28 undocks and lands on Earth in Kazakhstan. [src: (CNN)]
Sports
- 2026 Formula One World Championship
- 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix
- In auto racing, Formula One announces that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit will host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in October, under an agreement signed between Bahrain and Malaysia. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 All-Ireland Senior Football Championship, Sports-related curses
- In Gaelic football, the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship concludes with Mayo defeating Kerry in the final to end one of sport's longest-running droughts and a 75-year wait for the title. [src: (ABC News Australia)] [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Iraqi conflict
- Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
- Ahmad al-Hamidawi, leader of Kata'ib Hezbollah, announces that the group will suspend military activities in Iraq following the withdrawal of U.S. troops, with the exception of targeting hostile aircraft violating the country's airspace. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
- Israeli settlers shoot and kill a Palestinian man at his home in Yasuf, West Bank, and injure another. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian Su-35 fighter jet shoots down a Russian Mi-8 helicopter over Voronezh Oblast, Russia, in a friendly fire incident. All three crew members are killed. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces on a dormitory at the University of Kordofan in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, kills five people. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- Explosions caused by suspected drone strikes are reported in Ethiopia's capital of Addis Ababa, including one near the Ethiopian National Defense Force' headquarters. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Pakistan launches airstrikes in Afghanistan, claiming the killing of 22 Taliban fighters at two locations, while the Government of Afghanistan reports that nine women and children are killed in Kunar Province and Helmand Province by Pakistan airstrikes. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Disasters and accidents
- A medical helicopter transporting a patient crashes off the coast of Santa Catalina Island in Los Angeles County, California, United States, killing two people, injuring two others, and leaving one missing. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Ethiopian civil conflict, TPLF insurgency in Ethiopia
- Eritrea–Ethiopia relations
- Ethiopia closes its embassy in Eritrea and announces the expulsion of ten Eritrean diplomats from the country, after accusing its neighbour of financing the Tigray People's Liberation Front. [src: (AP)]
- Eritrea's foreign ministry announces that the country will cut off diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Egypt–Ethiopia relations
- A diplomat from Egypt is told to leave Ethiopia within 48 hours after being declared as persona non grata. [src: (Reuters)]
- The European Commission stops payments with immediate effect to Sierra Leone, which would have been €18 million for 2026, after the nation refused to cooperate with the extradition of drugs trafficker Jos Leijdekkers. [src: (Het Parool)]
Law and crime
- Censorship in Egypt, Human rights in Egypt
- Egyptian police are arresting six journalists from a fact-checking and investigative media outlet, accusing them of spreading misinformation on behalf of the banned Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
- British counter-terrorism police arrest a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national in Westminster, London, England, on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts linked to the RAF Fairford investigation. Officers also search two properties in the area. [src: (CNN)]
- Sentencing Act 2026
- Hundreds of prisoners begin leaving prison in England and Wales under an early release scheme by the British government to avoid overcapacity in prisons. More than 4,500 "low-risk" prisoners are expected to be released in the coming weeks. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Firstpost)]
- Former Malawian military chief Paul Valentino Phiri is arrested by Malawi's anti-corruption agency for allegedly trafficking weapons to Sudan during his tenure in June and July 2025. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- Two 18-year-old former students attack a secondary school in Torreón, Coahuila, Mexico, with knives and pyrotechnic devices, killing the vice-principal and injuring three people. Police arrest both suspects. [src: (AFP via RNZ)]
Politics and elections
- Immigration to Japan
- Japan tightens permanent residency requirements for foreign nationals, introducing above-average income and basic Japanese-language standards while raising application fees twentyfold as part of broader changes to immigration policy. [src: (AFP)]
- Gerardo Giovagnoli and William Casali are sworn in as the new Captains Regent of San Marino, succeeding Alice Mina and Vladimiro Selva. [src: (San Marino RTV)]
- Ousted Sudanese leader Omar al-Bashir is sent to a military hospital in Khartoum, Sudan, for medical treatment. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- SpaceX Crew-13 
- The SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station launches, carrying two NASA astronauts, one Roscosmos cosmonaut, and one Canadian Space Agency astronaut, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, United States. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 15
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- Saudi Arabia says that it has intercepted a missile intended for Medina. However, the Houthis denied launching a missile at the city. [src: (The Hill)] [src: (France 24)]
- The Houthis launch missiles against Al-Maashiq Palace, headquarters of the Presidential Leadership Council and official residence of President Rashad al-Alimi, in Aden, Yemen, killing five people and injuring 16. No member of the council is harmed in the attack. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- China–North Korea relations
- The New Yalu River Bridge connecting Dandong, China, and Sinuiju, North Korea, opens following a 12-year delay. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (NK News)]
- The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender. [src: (The Eastern Herald)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Peshawar school roof collapse
- A roof collapses at a school in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing 34 students and a teacher, and injuring 50 more people. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- Four people are killed fighting wildfires in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, after flames and thick smoke trapped them. Two others suffer serious burns. [src: (AFP)]
- Seven people are missing after a San Marino-flagged tanker catches fire off the coast of Romania amid recent drone attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea. Search and rescue operations are underway to locate the missing crew members. [src: (Politico)]
Health and environment
- The United Kingdom declares a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex after prolonged low rainfall left more than 80% of England in drought and major reservoirs below 20% capacity. [src: (AFP)]
International relations
- Germany–Iran relations, Antisemitism in 21st-century Germany, Iranian external operations
- A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentences a Danish national to eight years and six months in prison and an Afghan national to four years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, on behalf of Iran. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Silver Rail Elementary School shooting
- Three children and a teacher are killed in a mass school shooting at the Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, United States. Two other people are wounded. The perpetrator, a 16-year-old male, is shot and killed by a bystander. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Capital punishment in the United States
- U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Department of Defense has reversed its plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, scheduled for December 3. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (AP)]
- Argentine police arrest at least 25 people after clashes during a university funding protest in Buenos Aires, while eight police officers are injured. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Northern Irish politician and former Democratic Unionist Party leader Jeffrey Donaldson is sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sexual abuse and rape. The offences occurred between 1985 and 2008. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Swedish government formation
- The Riksdag votes against the appointment of Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson to repeat as Prime Minister of Sweden. Last 28 September, Andersson already returned her mandate to explore forming a new government. [src: (Anadolu Agency)]
Science and technology
- Astronomers discover the first green star, WD J1330+6435, according to a study published by RAS Techniques and Instruments. [src: (Popular Science)]
- At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027. To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Scientific American)]
Sports
- 2026 Major League Baseball season
- In baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS to advance to the 2026 World Series, their first since 1982. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 6
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
- The Houthis launches missiles against the airports of Najran and Jizan, in Saudi Arabia, causing material damages and wounding three people. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that the military has killed 4,000 militants who took part in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. [src: (The Jewish Chronicle)]
- Somali Civil War
- Piracy off the coast of Somalia
- Four Indonesian seamen return home after Puntland maritime police rescued 17 crew members from the hijacked oil tanker MT Honour 25. Somali pirates had held the crew for more than five months and killed five members. [src: (AFP)]
- Peruvian security crisis
- Three gunmen and a police officer are killed, and another officer is wounded, in a shootout during an operation against illegal miners in Inambari District, Tambopata province, Madre de Dios, Peru. Authorities seize 15 AKM rifles, a pistol, and five grenades. [src: (Evidencia de Perú )] [src: (Infobae )]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Two merchant ships are hit by drones of unknown origins off the coast of Bulgaria. One of the ships has sunk, leaving the crew missing. [src: (Reuters)]
- Boko Haram insurgency
- At least ten soldiers are killed by Islamic State gunmen during an attack at a military base in Kukawa, Borno State, Nigeria. Over 25 attackers are also killed in the shootout. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
- The merger between American media conglomerates Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery into Skydance takes effect. [src: (AFP)] [src: (CNN)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Kenya confirms its first imported case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebolavirus in Nairobi in a deceased male who traveled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Nairobi Hospital steps up its infection-control measures, tracing, and staff monitoring following Kenya's first imported case of Ebola. [src: (The Star Kenya)]
- Deforestation in Indonesia
- Indonesia halts a program to clear millions of hectares of forest for rice cultivation after achieving rice self-sufficiency, and plans instead to increase yields on existing farmland through improved agricultural methods. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
Law and crime
- 2026 European unrest
- Riots break out in Liège, Belgium, following a day of student protests, resulting in damaged shops and destroyed bus shelters in the city center. [src: (AA)] [src: (Le Soir )]
- August Hanning espionage case
- August Hanning, former head of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service, is arrested at his home in Nordwalde, North Rhine-Westphalia, after being charged by the country's Federal Public Prosecutor General with treason, espionage, and trading state secrets. A former aide of Hanning's is also arrested for aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
- A student is killed and seven others are injured in a mass stabbing at a middle school in Istanbul, Turkey. The suspect, a 15-year-old girl, is arrested. [src: (Turkiye Today)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Haitian general election, Haitian crisis
- Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council postpones presidential and legislative elections scheduled for December 13, citing technical, operational, and security requirements. [src: (AFP)]
- 2026 Kosovan presidential election
- The Kuvendi begins the procedure to elect a president on 6 October, finishing the voting process minutes after the constitutional deadline on midnight 7 October. Justina Pula is declared the next president of Kosovo. [src: (AFP via Gulf News)] [src: (Kosovo Online)]
- 2026 Latvian parliamentary election 
- Latvian president Edgars Rinkēvičs asks Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs to form the new Government. Kulbergs' party, the United List, won the plurality in the October 3 parliamentary elections. [src: (LSM)]
Science and technology
- OpenAI bulk release of mathematical papers
- OpenAI releases 377 results on open problems in mathematics in areas such as algebra, number theory, combinatorics and theoretical computer science. [src: (The New York Times)]
- 2026 Nobel Prizes
- Belgian physicist Francis Halzen from the University of Wisconsin–Madison is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his "decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin". [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 in archosaur paleontology
- The Royal Society Open Science reports the discovery of the Herugavialis cairensis crocodile species in the Mokattam Formation, which had also provided the rock to build the Great Sphinx in Egypt. [src: (CNN)] [src: (Phys.org)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- September 2026 United States strikes on Iran
- The United States carries out additional airstrikes against Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corp (IRGC) targets in Iran, in response to recent attempted attacks on commercial shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and on U.S. troops in the region, according to the U.S. Central Command. Five members of the IRGC Aerospace Force are killed in Kermanshah. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that his country is ready to return to the Islamabad Memorandum signed in June if the United States does the same amidst renewed fighting between the two countries. [src: (Fortune)]
- 2026 Kuhestak wedding airstrike
- Iranian state media reports that five civilians were killed and 63 more were wounded at a wedding party at a home in Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, during an American airstrike against Iranian military targets. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war
- Four people are killed in Israeli strikes during a ground operation in Gaza. Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that Israeli forces captured a senior Hamas internal security official in the operation. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- War against the Islamic State, Yemeni Civil War
- Abu Hudhayfah al-Ansari, the spokesperson for the Islamic State, is killed during a security operation by the Yemeni Armed Forces. [src: (Voice of Emirates)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes
- Ukrainian officials say that Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas killed at least 12 people, including an Indian national, and injure dozens, while damaging residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure. [src: (NDTV)]
- Colombian conflict
- A car bomb explodes outside a police station in Norte de Santander Department, Colombia, killing a person and wounding eleven more. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- The 75,000-seater Kingdome, built by the Christian sect Kingdom of Jesus Christ, opens in Davao City, Philippines, becoming the largest indoor arena in the world. It surpasses the 55,000-seater Philippine Arena in Bulacan. [src: (Manila Bulletin)] [src: (MindaNews)]
Business and economy
- Senegal hidden debt scandal
- The International Monetary Fund reaches a staff-level agreement with Senegal on a new US$2.2 billion, 36-month loan program supporting economic reforms after an earlier arrangement was suspended over previously unreported government debt. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Ghana begins requiring artisanal doré bars purchased by privately financed gold buyers to undergo domestic refining before export, with GoldBod considering export applications only after processing at approved refineries. [src: (Reuters)]
- Japan eases overtime enforcement by ending pressure on companies with special labor-management agreements to keep monthly overtime below 45 hours, as businesses face labor shortages. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- Nepal–South Korea relations
- South Korea's foreign ​ministry announces that the country will deploy a 44-member emergency relief team to Nepal to support search-and-rescue operations after flash floods hit the South Asian country. [src: (The Korea Herald)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Nepali Army reports that around 119 people have been rescued. [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Tropical Storm Edouard makes landfall on the Gulf Coast of the United States. [src: (CNN)]
- Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a speeding passenger van, with an Ipil–Pagadian route, crashes into a motorcycle and a wing van in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Four people are killed and more than ten others are injured when a car crashes into a gathering of government and military supporters in Mashhad, Razavi Khorasan, Iran. Traffic police arrest the driver and say the incident was unintentional. [src: (Reuters)]
- Six pilgrims are killed and 14 others sustain serious injuries after a pickup truck carrying devotees collides with a truck along an expressway in Palwal district, Haryana, India. [src: (The Times of India)]
Health and environment
- The New Zealand Conservation Department reports that the amount of critically endangered kākāpō have reached 325 in the country following the addition of 90 chicks, exceeding 300 for the first time in 75 years. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (NBC News)]
International relations
- Germany–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
- Germany raises its threat assessment to "high", orders the closure of Russia's consulate in Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, and the Russian House in Berlin, and tightens entry controls for Russian nationals after attributing the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Saxony, last month to Russia. [src: (CNN)]
- Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
- Peru's foreign ministry says that the country has cut off ties with Iran, accusing it of escalating the war in the Middle East. [src: (AP in Spanish)] [src: (Al-Arabiya)]
Law and crime
- Assassination of Charlie Kirk
- An American judge rules that the case against Tyler James Robinson, accused of murdering political activist Charlie Kirk in September 2025, can go to trial, citing sufficient probable cause. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- LGBTQ rights in the United States
- The U.S. Department of Justice files a lawsuit against the public schools district of Kansas City, Kansas, over its policies that allow transgender students to share their preferred name, gender, and pronouns with school staff. [src: (KCUR)] [src: (Reuters)]
- A Honduran judge dismisses a corruption case against former president Juan Orlando Hernández, ruling that he neither authorized nor managed the public funds allegedly diverted to finance his 2013 presidential campaign. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Mexican musician Jonathan Meléndez of the band Camilo Séptimo, his pregnant wife, their three-year-old daughter, a domestic worker, and their pet dog are shot dead in a penthouse outside Mexico City, while Meléndez's six-year-old son is found unharmed. Prosecutors arrest two suspects. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- Death and state funeral of Harald V
- Haakon VIII takes the oath as King of Norway before the Storting following the death of his father, Harald V. His daughter, Ingrid Alexandra, takes the oath as Crown Princess. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Nicaragua's National Assembly approves on first reading a constitutional amendment barring opposition parties from elections and extending presidential and other elected terms from six to seven years. A second legislative vote is required for ratification. [src: (Reuters)]
- Former British prime minister Keir Starmer resigns as a member of the House of Commons for his appointment to the Chiltern Hundreds; a by-election will be held to fill his parlimentary seat of Holborn and St Pancras. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)]
Science and technology
- Syria and weapons of mass destruction
- The International Atomic Energy Agency reports that Syria's former government under Bashar al-Assad failed to declare nuclear material and facilities, confirming that infrastructure at Deir ez-Zor is consistent with an unfinished nuclear reactor and identifying about 73 tonnes of natural uranium. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- The Turkish foreign ministry reports that Turkey has joined the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 71st country to do so. [src: (AA)] [src: (Firstpost)]
Sports
- 2026–27 NBA season
- In basketball, the NBA announces that the Los Angeles Clippers had violated the league salary cap by signing Kawhi Leonard in 2022 via a series of external dealings. Penalties include fines of US$30 million for the Clippers and $700,000 for Leonard, the loss of the Clippers' first-round picks in each draft from 2029 to 2033, and a one-year suspension for Clippers owner Steve Ballmer. [src: (AFP via Daily Tribune)] [src: (ESPN)]
- In baseball, the Los Angeles Angels of the MLB are sold to Stan Kroenke of Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for an unspecified price, ending 23 years of ownership by Arte Moreno. The deal is pending regulatory review and is expected to be complete by 2027. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 14
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives 
- Houthi forces seize control of the Hanish Islands in the Red Sea consolidating the group's control of the strategic sea lane off Yemen's western coast. [src: (AP)]
- Houthi forces advance towards the PLC-controlled cities of Marib and Taiz with heavy clashes underway. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Iranian support for the Houthis
- Gulf states call off planned peace talks with Iran in response to Houthi ballistic missile attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemeni government forces. [src: (Reuters)]
- Mexican drug war
- At least seven suspected gunmen are killed and two others are detained after an armed group attacks Nuevo León police and soldiers in General Treviño, Mexico. Police later arrest three additional suspects. [src: (La Jornada in Spanish)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudan's Popular Congress Party and Sudan Liberation Movement faction led by Abdul Wahid al-Nur agree to broaden talks aimed at ending the three-year civil war in the country. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Arts and culture
- 78th Primetime Emmy Awards
- American actress Jean Smart wins a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series for her role in Hacks, becoming the first actress to win for every season of a show. [src: (Entertainment Weekly)] [src: (Variety)]
- Canadian–American actor Michael J. Fox wins the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award for his contributions to research and advocacy on Parkinson's disease. [src: (Reuters)]
- American comedy horror television series Widow's Bay wins 14 Emmys including Outstanding Comedy Series, surpassing the record set by The Studio last year. [src: (The Hollywood Reporter)] [src: (Los Angeles Times)]
Business and economy
- Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Catholic Church
- Pope Leo XIV restores salaries for cardinals and senior Vatican City officials to pre-COVID-19-pandemic levels, ending reductions introduced by Pope Francis in 2021. The change took effect September 1, 2026, without retroactive compensation. [src: (The Sun)]
- Nigeria's Dangote Group launches an initial public offering (IPO) of 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 (US$0.40) each, seeking to raise about ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) to fund the expansion of the Dangote refinery in Lekki, Lagos State. The sale is set to become Africa's biggest IPO. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd announce that they will sail more container ships through the Suez Canal. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- Indonesia extends the search for eight people, including five journalists, after their speedboat disappeared in the Sunda Strait during a reporting mission on Anak Krakatoa's eruption a week prior. Police await test results to identify a body found on Enggano Island. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
Health and environment
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- The World Food Programme reports that Sudan's Darfur region is having its driest rainy season since the 1980s, worsening famine conditions amidst the ongoing civil war. [src: (AFP via Free Malaysia Today)]
- Chile becomes the first country in South America to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies, with the World Health Organization confirming the milestone. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Separatism in the United Kingdom, Decolonization
- The First Ministers of Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales meet in Cardiff at a summit to call for their independence from the United Kingdom. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Law and crime
- Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
- United States district judge F. Dennis Saylor IV of Massachusetts postpones new rules limiting stays for international students and journalists, preventing the measures from taking effect while a legal challenge proceeds. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election
- Parliamentary elections are held in the Bangsamoro autonomous region, Philippines, its first since its establishment in 2018. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Science and technology
- Militarisation of space
- The United States confirms for the first time that it has deployed a weapon in Earth's orbit. Air Force secretary Troy Meink says the highly classified weapon is necessary to "safeguard U.S. forces" against potential enemy action. [src: (BBC News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 16
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Twenty-one people are killed, 45 are injured, and about 100 others are missing after a residential building in Gaza City collapses after it was previously hit by an Israeli airstrike. Twelve children are among the fatalities. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 Americana Music Honors & Awards
- The Americana Music Honors & Awards are held at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tennessee, United States, with the Heartbreakers performing for the first time since lead vocalist Tom Petty's death in 2017. [src: (The Independent)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- Guatemala announces food aid for about 1.2 million families affected by severe El Niño-related drought, which damages crops and livestock across the Dry Corridor. The programme distributes maize, beans, and rice with World Food Programme support. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- At least 82 people are killed when a gold mine explodes in West Kordofan, Sudan, an area under control of the Rapid Support Forces. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Sky News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 United Kingdom heatwaves
- The United Kingdom records its second-best butterfly season in 16 years amidst record heat waves in the country. [src: (The Independent)]
- Fiji declares HIV a national crisis after reporting 2,016 new diagnoses in 2025, sixteen times the 2019 total. The government estimates that one in 60 adults lives with HIV and expands testing, prevention, and treatment services. [src: (AFP via New Straits Times)]
- In a study published by the Nature Medicine journal, scientists report that the PANXEON blood test helps detect pancreatic cancer at early stages and treat the disease before it spreads. [src: (Scientific American)] [src: (Discover)]
International relations
- Canada–European Union relations
- European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen invites Canada to become the first associate member of the European Union amidst the ongoing trade war between Canada and the United States. [src: (CNBC)]
- International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- The United States House of Representatives passes a bipartisan sanctions bill that imposes sanctions on Russia's energy revenues, financial institutions, officials, and shadow fleet, while authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The bill will head to president Donald Trump's desk for his signature for it to become law. [src: (Kyiv Independent)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The first summit between South Korea and the five countries of Central Asia is held in Seoul. [src: (Euronews)] [src: (AFP via Korea Times)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Law and crime
- North Korea–South Korea relations
- Inter-Korean Liaison Office bombing
- A district court in Seoul, South Korea, orders North Korea to pay KRW44.6 billion (US$32.5 million) in damages for destroying the Inter-Korean Liaison Office in Kaesong in 2020, in South Korea's first damages lawsuit against North Korea. [src: (AFP via CNA)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Human rights in Macau
- Macau begins its first closed-door national security trial against former legislator Au Kam San, who faces charges including subversion of state power and alleged ties with foreign groups and media outlets. He faces up to 25 years in prison. [src: (AFP via RTL Today)]
- War crimes in the Kosovo War
- The Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentences former prime minister Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison after convicting him on charges of murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention committed during the Kosovo War. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election
- The Philippine Commission on Elections proclaims all 78 elected members of the Bangsamoro Parliament, with four parties given all seats for party representation. The Bangsamoro Federalist Party, earning most of the seats, fails to secure a majority, leading to a hung parliament. Meanwhile, six sectoral seats are given to the United Bangsamoro Justice Party. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Manila Bulletin)]
Science and technology
- Discoveries of exoplanets
- Astronomers confirm the existence of Elias 2-24 b, the youngest known exoplanet, which is less than one million years old and located approximately 450 light-years from Earth. The discovery was observed through the W.M. Keck Observatory in Mauna Kea, Hawaii, U.S., using a coronagraph. [src: (Space.com)]
- NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter discovers a recently formed crater on the moon larger than the Colosseum in Rome, Italy. [src: (Phys.org)]
- A study published by the Science Advances scientific journal find that the Tyrannosaurus had a temperature of . [src: (Scientific American)]
Sports
- In association football, Clearlake Capital buys out Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's stakes to gain full control of Premier League club Chelsea. The deal is valued at around £950 million (€1.1 billion) for the 25% share. Chelsea is now worth about £5 billion (€5.8 billion). [src: (BBC Sport)] [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (ESPN)]
- The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) announces that its finals will move from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina, United States, for three years beginning in 2027. The WTA also relocates its global headquarters from St. Petersburg, Florida, to Charlotte. [src: (BBC)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 23
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The United States Central Command says that the U.S. military has redirected 115 commercial vessels since the reinstatement of its blockade on July 14. [src: (Gulf News)]
- An Indian wiper is killed during an attack on the bulk carrier MV Cape Dao near the Strait of Hormuz, with Oman's navy confirming that 27 crew members have been evacuated. [src: (AFP and Reuters via Arab News)] [src: (The Indian Express)]
- Iran reopens schools and universities after months of closures caused by the war. About 16.5 million schoolchildren begin the new academic year, with reopening ceremonies held across the country. [src: (AFP via Channels Television)]
- Acting United States Navy secretary Hung Cao reports that eight sailors on the have attempted suicide during its long deployment including during the Iran war. [src: (BBC News)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) seizes several airports in Tigray, while clashes are ongoing in the nearby regions of Afar and Amhara. The TPLF says that it has started a "defensive war" against the federal government of Ethiopia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kharkiv strikes, Kyiv strikes, Odesa strikes
- Russian drone and missile attacks across Ukraine kill at least eight civilians, including six agricultural workers in Kharkiv Oblast and two people in Kyiv, while strikes also hit Odesa. Ukraine says it intercepts or suppresses 119 of 161 drones. [src: (AP)]
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Poland deploys fighter jets into its airspace after a Russian helicopter intruded near Braniewo, Warmian–Masurian Voivodeship. [src: (Chronicle Live)]
- Colombian conflict
- Threats and attacks by the Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada (ACSN) bring Santa Marta, Magdalena Department, Colombia, to a standstill, closing businesses and public transport. The group orders the shutdown after security forces kill 13 ACSN members. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Communal conflicts in Nigeria
- Fifteen people, including a village head, are killed in an armed ethnic clash in Bagudo, Kebbi State, Nigeria. Six suspects are arrested following the attack. [src: (Daily Post)]
- Islamist insurgency in Niger
- Islamic State militants kill at least 20 gendarmes in an ambush near Abala and Filingué in Tillabéri Region, Niger. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war, United States sanctions against Iran
- Iranian airlines suspend services to Azerbaijan, Baghdad, Georgia, Muscat, and Qatar, after new U.S. sanctions target Iran's aviation sector. [src: (AFP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Tropical Storm Fay re-emerges as a tropical depression with a sustained wind of 35 mph amidst a unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño. [src: (Sun Sentinel)]
Health and environment
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- The Atacama Desert in Chile reports blossoms of flowers amidst the ongoing El Nino event in the Pacific. [src: (Phys.org)]
International relations
- Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
- Sudanese civil war
- Africa–United States relations
- The United States and African Union hold the first joint Quad-Quintet talks at the United Nations General Assembly sidelines in a effort to end the ongoing civil war in Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Belarus–Poland relations
- Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski and Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov meet at the United Nations General Assembly, making it the first meeting between Poland and Belarus in a decade. [src: (UA News)] [src: (Notes from Poland)]
- Azerbaijan–France relations
- Azerbaijani president Ilham Aliyev pardons a French national who served a 10-year prison sentence for espionage, and orders his release as one of 20 pardoned prisoners. [src: (BBC News)]
- Cross-strait relations
- Taiwan's coast guard increases patrol capacity around the disputed Pratas Island in the South China Sea by stationing a new 100-tonne patrol boat and regularly deploying larger vessels, citing increased China Coast Guard activity near the Taiwan-controlled outpost. [src: (Reuters)]
- North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war, South Korea–Ukraine relations
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukraine transferred two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea after capturing them in Kursk Oblast, Russia, in January 2025. [src: (UPI)]
Law and crime
- Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases
- A court in New York, United States, sentences former film producer Harvey Weinstein to 15 years in prison for committing a criminal sexual act against former production assistant Miriam Haley. [src: (BBC News)]
- Mexican drug war, missing persons in Mexico
- Congresswoman Margarita López Pérez reports that, since 2021, Searching Mothers have found around 1,600 milk teeth, among other skeletal remains, in a mass grave in Zacapu, Michoacán. The state prosecutor's office denies having reports on the case. [src: (Guillermo Ortega)]
- War crimes in the Myanmar civil war
- Human Rights Watch reports that women held as political prisoners in Myanmar face torture, sexual violence, and inadequate medical care. The group says more than 6,600 women and 640 children are among over 30,000 political prisoners detained since 2021. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Israeli legislative election
- The Central Elections Committee votes to disqualify Ra'am and all parties on the Joint List from running, alleging they promoted terrorism against Israel. Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh and MK Ofer Cassif are also specifically barred from running. [src: (Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Moroccan general election
- Moroccans vote to elect all 395 members of the House of Representatives. [src: (AP)]
- Second impeachment of Sara Duterte
- The Philippine Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, rules that only senator-judges able to participate count toward the conviction threshold in vice president Sara Duterte's trial, reducing the required votes from 16 to 14. [src: (Reuters)]
- The United Kingdom establishes a National Centre for Information Defence to detect and counter foreign disinformation, including AI-generated content. Prime Minister Andy Burnham says the centre will address disinformation attacks to states such as Russia. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Science and technology
- 2026 OpenAI infiltration of Medicare
- Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese says that an OpenAI-deployed agent accessed public and restricted files on a Medicare database during testing in June. OpenAI notified the government in September, while investigations continue into the breach. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Croatia joins the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 74th country to do so. [src: (Croatia Week)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- North Korea at the 2026 Asian Games, Weightlifting at the 2026 Asian Games
- North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum wins gold in the women's 49kg category at the 2026 Asian Games while setting three world records: 94kg in the snatch, 121kg in the clean and jerk, and 215kg overall. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 3
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war, United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war
- Iran's military launches drones and missiles on Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, targeting United States military facilities and equipment to retaliate for the recent U.S. bombardment of Iran that killed at least 19 people. [src: (AFP via South China Morning Post)]
- 2026 Kuhestak wedding airstrike
- U.S. vice president JD Vance says that the country will investigate its military strike against a wedding in Bandar Sirik that killed five people. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
- Israel releases prisoner Malek Ghazi and hands him over to the Lebanese army, the first release since the war started in March, as part of an effort to revive peace talks. [src: (AP)] [src: (Arab News)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensive
- The Houthis launch an offensive in western Yemen, clashing with the Yemeni Armed Forces and aiming to reach and cut the road linking Taiz to Al-Makha district. Fourteen balistic missiles and several drones are launched in Taiz and Hodeidah. At least 18 Houthi fighters and 13 government troops are killed in the clashes. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo–Ukrainian war
- Kharkiv Oblast campaign
- Russian forces say they have captured several settlements in northeastern Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, encircling Ukrainian forces. [src: (ISW)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudanese refugee crisis
- The International Organization for Migration reports the first operation of a voluntary repatriation flight for stranded migrants in Khartoum, Sudan, since the war started three years ago. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Colombian conflict
- A Colombian judge orders president Abelardo de la Espriella's government to suspend airstrikes on guerrilla camps in the Guaviare Department when intelligence indicated that minors may be present, after recent bombings killed at least three teenagers. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Insurgency in Cabo Delgado
- At least one person is killed and no less than 11 people are abducted by ISM militants in an attack on a hunting camp in Niassa Province, Mozambique. [src: (AP)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- Five people are killed and several other residents are abducted during a bandit attack in Kebbe, Sokoto State, Nigeria. [src: (Daily Post Nigeria)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- 2026 East Malaysia haze, Endangerment of orangutans
- Authorities in Indonesia rescue a mother orangutan and her baby from wildfire smoke on the island of Borneo. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (The Borneo Post)]
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- United Arab Emirates president Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan announces that the country will deploy an emergency relief mission to Nepal to support people affected by the deadly floods and landslides. [src: (Gulf News)]
- At least 37 people are killed after inhaling petroleum fumes while allegedly siphoning fuel from an illegally tapped pipeline in Rivers State, Nigeria. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Six crew members are referred to court as part of the investigation into the ship collision in the Sea of Marmara yesterday, while the search continues for the ten Turkish crew members aboard the sunken MV Tuğberk İmamoğlu cargo ship. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 East Malaysia haze
- Malaysia's disaster agency, meteorological agency, and air force launch cloud-seeding operations in Sarawak to reduce haze and increase water reserves. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Syrian chemical weapons program, Use of chemical weapons in the Syrian civil war
- Officials at a United Nations Security Council meeting say that Syria has started the process of destroying clandestine chemical weapons from former president Bashar al-Assad's regime. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Germany–Russia relations
- 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
- Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov says that Russia will close Goethe-Institut cultural centers in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Yekaterinburg in response to Germany closing Russia's consulate in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin following the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Tacloban school shooting, 2026 Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting
- The Philippine education department initiates nationwide school safety drills to prepare students and staff for armed intruders, involving police and emergency responders after two school shooting incidents. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- A court in Moscow, Russia, places children's hospice founder Lida Moniava under judicial supervision, imposing a nightly curfew, internet ban, and contact restrictions over a 2023 post prosecutors said spread false information about the military. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2025–2026 United States redistricting
- In the United States, the Supreme Court of Missouri blocks the use of a congressional map intended to favor Republicans, despite the map having already been used for primary elections in the state. A referendum on the 2025 map will appear on the ballot for the November election in the state. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, the latest version of ChatGPT. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)] [src: (Axios)]
- 2026 in spaceflight
- The BepiColombo begins its final mission to Mercury, eight years after its launch by the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency. [src: (Space.com)]
- NASA discovers a 10–sided pattern on the south pole of Saturn using its Hubble Space Telescope from the Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, United States. [src: (The Peninsula)] [src: (ScienceDaily)]
- Ig Nobel Prize
- The 36th Ig Nobel Prize ceremony is held in Zürich, Switzerland. The ceremony, normally held in the Greater Boston area, was the first held outside the United States due to due to safety concerns about international visitors entering the country. [src: (Ars Technica)]
Sports
- In association football, the French Football Federation upholds Bordeaux's relegation to Régional 1, the sixth tier of the French football league system, rejecting the club's request for reinstatement in National 2 following its exclusion from national competitions over financial concerns. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

Progress MS-35 (Russian: Прогресс МC-35), Russian production No. 463, identified by NASA as Progress 96, is a Progress cargo spacecraft mission by Roscosmos to resupply the International Space Station (ISS) launched in September 2026.
## Cargo
Each Progress mission delivers pressurized and unpressurized cargo to the station. The pressurized section carries consumables such as food, along with equipment for maintenance and scientific research. The unpressurized section contains tanks of fuel, drinking water, and gases to replenish the onboard atmosphere, which are transferred to the station through automated systems. Progress MS-35 carried 2,600 kg of cargo.

Skyroot Aerospace Private Limited is an Indian private aerospace manufacturer and commercial launch service provider headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana. The company was founded by two former ISRO scientists, Pawan Kumar Chandana, and Naga Bharath Daka.
On 18 November 2022, Skyroot became the first private company in India to launch a suborbital rocket, Vikram-S. On 18 July 2026, Skyroot successfully launched India's first private orbital class rocket Vikram-1 into orbit, making India the third country with a private orbital launch capability after the U.S. and China.
## History
### Founding and early development
Initial logo of Skyroot Aerospace
Skyroot Aerospace was founded in 2018 by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka. The company sought to develop commercially competitive launch vehicles for the global small satellite market.
The company emerged during a period of increasing government support for private participation in India's space industry. Reforms introduced in 2020 enabled private firms to access certain ISRO facilities and created a regulatory framework under the oversight of Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe).
During its initial years, Skyroot focused on developing launch vehicle technologies, and manufacturing processes aimed at reducing launch costs and production times. The company adopted technologies including carbon-composite structures, 3D printing, and modular launch vehicle designs.
### Mission Prarambh
Pawan Kumar Chandana (CEO & CTO) and Naga Bharath Daka (COO) (standing on left and right respectively of Union minister Jitendra Singh in middle) on the eve of successful Vikram-S launch
On 18 November 2022, Skyroot launched Vikram-S, a suborbital rocket, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota under a mission designated Prarambh (lit. 'the beginning'). Vikram-S used the existing launch pad and ground support system infrastructure provided by the government of India at Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC). The mission reached an altitude of approximately 89.5 km (55.6 mi) and marked the first successful launch of a privately developed rocket from India. The event was widely regarded as a milestone in the development of India's private space industry.
### Expansion and funding
Following the Vikram-S mission, Skyroot raised capital from domestic and international investors. On 30 October 2023, the company announced that it had raised US$27.5 million in a pre-Series C funding round led by Temasek Holdings that brought its cumulative funding to approximately US$95 million.
On 21 January 2025, the Government of Telangana signed a MoU with Skyroot Aerospace at the World Economic Forum to establish a private rocket manufacturing, integration, and testing facility in Telangana with an estimated investment of ₹500 crore (US$52 million).
On 7 May 2026, following its latest funding round of approximately US$60 million, Skyroot Aerospace crossed US$1.1 billion in valuation. With this, it became India's first space-tech unicorn.
### Mission Aagaman
On 2 July 2026, the company announced a launch window from 12 July to 4 August 2026 for its first orbital mission, 'Mission Aagaman' (lit. 'the arrival'), using the Vikram-1 launch vehicle from SDSC. The mission is intended to demonstrate the rocket's propulsion, guidance, and stage-separation systems while carrying domestic and international payloads. 
On 18 July 2026, the launch was successful, with the mission meeting all its objectives and deploying payload at an altitude of 450 km (280 mi). Skyroot became the first private Indian company to successfully reach space in its first attempt. This made India the third country in the world after the U.S. and China to have rocket launch by private company.
### Other launches
On 14 October 2026, Reflect Orbital announced a contract with Skyroot Aerospace for two dedicated satellite launches. The agreement includes one flight aboard Vikram-1 and a second on Vikram-1U, an upgraded variant equipped with strap-on boosters that increases payload capacity from 350 to 550 kg (770 to 1,210 lb) to LEO.
Financial terms and specific launch dates were not publicly disclosed. The launches will deploy Reflect Orbital's planned satellite constellation, which is designed to redirect sunlight to specific locations on Earth using orbital mirrors. The company intends for the technology to extend the operating hours of solar farms and assist in industrial and search-and-rescue operations.
The partnership occurred amidst a global shortage of commercial launch capacity, largely attributed to the phaseout of SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket, Reflect Orbital CEO Ben Nowack cited this industry-wide capacity shortage and the need for schedule certainty as primary factors in securing the dedicated flights with Skyroot.

Vikram-1

Main article: Vikram-1
Schematic representation of Vikram-1
Vikram-1 is a four-stage small-lift launch vehicle. The first launch of Vikram-1 took place on 18 July 2026.
Vikram-2
- 
Main article: Vikram-2
Vikram-2 is an under-development small-lift launch vehicle. The rocket will use an upper stage cryogenic engine powered by the Dhawan-series rocket engine.
### Rocket engines
#### Solid rocket motors
##### Kalam-100
The Kalam-100 (named after A. P. J. Abdul Kalam) is the third-stage solid rocket motor of Vikram-1. The stage produces a peak vacuum thrust of approximately 100 kN (or ~10 tons). In April 2025, Skyroot conducted successful static firing of Kalam-100 featuring an advanced flex-nozzle system for thrust vector control. The test lasted over 102 seconds and formed part of the qualification programme for the maiden orbital flight of Vikram-1.
##### Kalam-250
The Kalam-250 is the second-stage solid rocket motor of Vikram-1. for the second stage of the Vikram-1 launch vehicle. It was successfully static-tested on 27 March 2024 at ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre, validating its 85-second burn and critical propulsion systems.
##### Kalam-1200
The Kalam-1200 is the first-stage solid rocket motor of Vikram-1. On 8 August 2025, Skyroot Aerospace successfully conducted the first static test of the Kalam-1200 solid rocket motor at SDSC, Sriharikota. The 110 second test validated the booster of the Vikram-1.
#### Earth-storable rocket engine
- 
Main article: Raman (rocket engine)
##### Raman engine
Raman (named after C. V. Raman) is a liquid-fuel upper stage engine of Vikram-1. The upper stage engine will be used in a cluster of four Raman-1, one Raman-2, and four Raman Mini in the fourth stage of the Vikram-1 rocket, which are capable of producing the total thrust of 5.26 kilonewtons (1,180 lbf) in vacuum.
#### Cryogenic rocket engines
##### Dhawan-I
On 25 September 2020, Skyroot Aerospace unveiled the Dhawan-I (named after Satish Dhawan) upper stage cryogenic engine that will power heavier-lift systems such as Vikram-2. This is India's first privately developed small cryogenic engine running on liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquid oxygen (LOX). Dhawan-I is 3D printed and designed with a regenerative cooling configuration. The engine is made by using superalloys.
##### Dhawan-II
On 5 April 2023, Skyroot announced the successful completion of a 200-second endurance static-fire test of its Dhawan-II engine, showcasing the viability of large-scale additive manufacturing for cryogenic propulsion.
##### Dhawan-III
The Dhawan-III engine represents an evolution of the earlier Dhawan-I and Dhawan-II engines, incorporating improvements aimed at future reusable launch vehicles and advanced upper-stage propulsion systems. In February 2026, Skyroot announced that Dhawan-III had successfully completed a 145-second endurance static-fire test. The firing was conducted on an indigenous mobile test stand designed and built in-house by the company. The test was intended to validate the engine's performance, combustion stability, and operational reliability over an extended duration.
## Facilities
Skyroot Aerospace has modern facilities for designing, building, testing, and assembling rockets and their components. These facilities help the company develop launch vehicles, test rocket engines, prepare missions, and support commercial satellite launches with advanced engineering and technology.
### MAX-Q
On 24 October 2023, the largest private integrated rocket development facility in India was unveiled by Skyroot Aerospace. It is situated next to the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport and spans 60,000 square feet. With space for about 300 personnel, this facility will host Skyroot's integrated design, manufacturing, and testing infrastructure for developing rockets. 
### Infinity Campus
On 27 November 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Infinity Campus of Skyroot Aerospace. Spread across 200,000 square feet in Hyderabad, this facility will be able to design, manufacture, integrate, and test a number of launch vehicles and produce one orbital rocket each month.
## Industry collaboration
An agreement has been signed by Nibe Space, a division of Nibe Defence and Aerospace on 9 September 2024, with Skyroot Aerospace, AgniKul Cosmos, Centum Electronics, SpaceFields, Sisir Radar, CYRAN AI Solutions, and Larsen & Toubro for the launch of India's first constellation of multi-sensor, all-weather, high-revisit Earth observation satellites.
On 25 June 2025, Skyroot Aerospace and Axiom Space signed an MoU to work together to increase access to LEO. Skyroot Aerospace and Axiom Space will look into orbital and launch systems that are integrated for next trips to Axiom Station and beyond. The two businesses intend to look into potential joint ventures for the construction of space infrastructure. By connecting Axiom's under-construction commercial space station and other LEO projects with Skyroot's upcoming Vikram-1 launch capability, the partnership hopes to create a new logistics corridor for research payloads, orbital data-center nodes, and upcoming commercial missions.
On 7 October 2026, Skyroot Aerospace and Brazilian company Concert Technologies SA signed an MoU for development of an launch vehicle capable of carrying at least 100 kg (220 lb) payload to LEO. The initiative seeks to develop this rocket as intermediate solution between Brazilian MLBR and Vikram-1. Concert Technologies is a consortium member of the MLBR.
